title: CROWDShield Venue Telemetry Frame
description:
TIER 3 of the CROWDShield state model: high-frequency observations over an existing venue topology. Companion to venue-graph.schema.json.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE DOCUMENT. A venue topology carries polygon geometry, capacities and configuration - kilobytes to megabytes, and constant for the whole event. Telemetry changes several times per second. Embedding one in the other would mean re-serialising, re-transmitting and re-parsing immutable geometry on every tick, which is the dominant avoidable cost in a system like this. Separating them means the per-tick payload is a few hundred bytes of numbers per zone, which is also precisely what makes SPEC §7's bandwidth and cost claims true and what lets the pipeline survive a poor network (FR-140).

CONTENTS ARE MEASUREMENTS, NOT CONCLUSIONS. A frame carries what a sensing source can compute on its own. It deliberately excludes:
  - quantities requiring a topology join (occupancy ratio, edge utilisation) - the consumer computes these,
  - detections (bottleneck, blockage, counterflow, surge) - outputs of the Detection layer,
  - risk score, severity, Time-To-Critical, recommendations - outputs of the Risk and Recommendation engines.
Holding that line keeps the venue model from becoming a god-object and keeps the deterministic risk core auditable (SPEC §13).

ORDERING AND REPLAY. `sequence` is strictly increasing per (venue_id, event_id). Gaps signal loss; duplicates are idempotent and MUST be discarded by frame_id (SPEC FR-142, FR-143).

frame_id.description: Globally unique, stable identifier for this frame. The idempotency key: a frame replayed from an offline buffer after reconnection carries the same frame_id and MUST be deduplicated, not double-counted (SPEC FR-142).

topology_binding.description: Binds this frame to the EXACT topology revision it was computed against. Without this, an administrator editing a capacity mid-event would silently invalidate cached adjacency and capacity indices and make risk scores from before and after the edit incomparable, with no way to detect it. A consumer whose loaded topology hash differs MUST refuse the frame or reload the topology.

observed_at.description: Instant the observations describe. Distinct from emitted_at: an edge node that buffered through an outage emits late but still describes the earlier instant, and conflating the two would silently backdate or postdate the whole timeline (SPEC FR-143, FR-147).

sequence.description: Strictly increasing per (venue_id, event_id). Enables gap detection and correct ordering of out-of-order arrivals after reconnection.

frame_type.description:
`full` - state for every monitored entity; safe to use as a cold-start baseline.
`delta` - only entities whose state changed since the previous sequence; smaller, but requires an established baseline. A consumer joining mid-stream MUST wait for a `full` frame.

evaluation_interval_ms.description: Nominal interval this frame represents. Lets a consumer distinguish a genuinely slower cadence from dropped frames.

system_mode.description: Operating mode of the emitting pipeline. `degraded` = reduced source coverage; `local_only` = control-room-local operation with the cloud unreachable. Surfaced to operators as the degraded-mode banner (SPEC FR-144) and used to lower confidence automatically (FR-145).

coverage.description: Self-assessment of input completeness for this frame. The honest basis for system-wide confidence: a frame covering three of twelve monitored zones must not present as authoritative.

allOf.title: A full frame must actually carry zone state

provenance.description: Drives the per-zone Data Integrity Badge (SPEC N-9 / FR-089). `simulated` is a first-class value, not a debug flag: the demo runs mixed real and simulated sources and the UI must label each honestly.

zone_state.description: Observed state of one zone at observed_at. Field semantics are identical to venue-graph.schema.json#/$defs/zone_current_state; this is the authoritative carrier and that one is a denormalised mirror.

observed_at.description: Per-zone observation time, when it differs from the frame's. Sources rarely tick in lockstep, and averaging across a spread of observation times without recording it is a quiet way to smear a fast-moving trend.

count_uncertainty_persons.description: Plus/minus band on person_count_estimate. Density regression at high occupancy under-counts in a known, direction-biased way (SPEC AI-1 failure modes), so a point estimate alone overstates what we know.

instability_index.description: SPEC N-1. Proxy for crowd pressure. Unbounded above; thresholds uncalibrated.

device_sample_count.description: Number of consenting devices contributing to this zone's movement statistics. Load-bearing for honesty in two ways: phone-derived signals are penetration-biased so absolute counts must never be inferred from them (SPEC §12), and the Differential Immobility Anomaly needs a minimum neighbour sample before a crowd baseline is meaningful at all (FR-133).

edge_state.description: Observed state of one connection. Carries MEASURED throughput only - utilisation against capacity is computed by the Bottleneck Physics Engine, which owns the topology join.

measured_flow_per_minute.description: Persons per minute observed in the edge's nominal FORWARD direction (source_zone -> target_zone).

measured_flow_per_minute_reverse.description: Persons per minute observed against the nominal direction. Non-zero alongside a non-zero forward flow is the definition of counterflow (SPEC FR-027); sustained reverse flow where forward is expected is reverse crowd movement (FR-026).

counterflow_fraction.description: Share of total observed flow moving against the dominant direction, 0 to 1.

flow_measurement_method.description: `direct` = measured at the connection. `inferred_from_occupancy` = back-computed from adjacent zone occupancy change, materially less reliable and never to be presented as equivalent. `unavailable` = unmonitored; the engine must report UNKNOWN for this edge rather than assume it is healthy (SPEC AI-4 failure modes).

dynamic_state.description: Current Tier 2 operational position, included here when it changed within this frame so that consumers holding a hydrated view stay consistent without a separate lookup. The authoritative record remains the audited transition log.

control_point_state.description: Current position of an operator-toggleable control. Low-frequency: appears in a frame only on change, or in every `full` frame as a baseline.

confirmed_by_responder_id.description: Present once a field responder has physically confirmed the change (SPEC FR-123). Until then the state is an intention, not a fact, and the simulation should treat it as such.
